content: Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration cannot be avoided, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration cannot be avoided, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat is known to significantly prolong the QT interval, and its prescribing information advises against use with drugs that also prolong the QTc interval. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration cannot be avoided, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration cannot be avoided, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir and pimavanserin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pimozide by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current pirtobrutinib dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitor use. Once the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor has been discontinued for five half-lives, resume pirtobrutinib at the dose taken before initiating the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current pirtobrutinib dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitor use. Once the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor has been discontinued for five half-lives, resume pirtobrutinib at the dose taken before initiating the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Lopinavir and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pitolisant by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases the levels of pomalidomide by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir also increases pomalidomide levels through the same mechanisms. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ponatinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ponatinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of propafenone by interfering with hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism and decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quazepam by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir also increases quazepam levels through the same mechanism. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ritonavir increases quinidine levels by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of quinidine by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of quinine by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir also increases quinine levels through the same mechanism. Quinine prescribing information recommends avoiding this combination. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir also increases ranolazine levels through the same mechanism. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin, and this combination may increase creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Lopinavir also increases red yeast rice levels through the same mechanism. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3–5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by other mechanisms (refer to comments). Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Resmetirom is an OATP1B1/3 substrate, and coadministration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors should be avoided. Ritonavir increases the levels of revefenacin by other mechanisms (refer to comments). Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transport inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to the active metabolite of revefenacin. Coadministration is not recommended. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir and ribociclib both prolong the QTc interval. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifapentine decreases ritonavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir also increases rimegepant levels through the same mechanisms. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use of rivaroxaban with combined P-glycoprotein and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, as this combination may significantly increase rivaroxaban levels and bleeding risk. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir also increases romidepsin levels through the same mechanism. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of roflumilast by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir increases the levels of rosuvastatin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases rosuvastatin toxicity through other mechanisms (refer to comments). OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the ruxolitinib starting dose to 10 mg BID if platelet count is ≥100 x 10^9/L and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are used concurrently. Avoid use if platelet counts are <100 x 10^9/L. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the ruxolitinib starting dose to 10 mg BID if platelet count is ≥100 x 10^9/L and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are used concurrently. Avoid use if platelet counts are <100 x 10^9/L. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the selumetinib dose taken before initiating the inhibitor. Sertraline and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Sevoflurane and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
